name: Decision-Maker Selector
description: Select decision-makers from fetched people records using word-boundary role matching on job titles, then emit ONE entity-keyed leadership-roster item whose text_content is pre-formatted prose (one 'Name — Title' per line). Complements the Bright Data LinkedIn-people Search provider: server-side `includes` is a substring match that cannot select titles cleanly (CTO matches 'director'), so role selection happens here, client-side. Step-5 reads only item.text_content, so the roster is ADDED as prose rather than filtered.
usage_notes: Runs on people records (e.g. LinkedIn profiles fetched by Step-3 api-fetcher). Matches each item's title field against a configurable role list using WORD-BOUNDARY regexes, so 'CTO' never matches 'director'/'factory'. Records with null / empty / emoji / slogan titles match nothing and are dropped. Two further, independently-diagnosable drops refine precision: (1) the company anchor rejects a matched title that names an organisation other than the target company or a derived alias ('Founder of SR Collection', 'Head of QA at RokkerX'); (2) the creative-title filter rejects creative roles that match 'Director of X' but are not executives ('Director of Photography'). The surviving decision-makers are folded into ONE item per entity, keyed on entity_name (item_key), whose text_content is a leadership roster the writer reads as prose. When zero decision-makers survive, no roster item is emitted (an empty roster is worse than none). Operation is `add`: the roster joins the pool alongside the scraped pages. The name field must be readable at the top level of the pool item (api-fetcher promotes name + current_company_name from the provider field_map); requires_columns cannot deliver it because name lives inside the stringified data_json blob and hydration is 1:1 by item_key. The role list is fully configurable; nothing is baked into code.

options.name: roles
options.label: Roles to keep (one per line: Role | phrase1, phrase2)
options.description: Each line is a role label and the title phrases that identify it. Phrases are matched with word boundaries and case-insensitively, so acronyms are safe (CTO will not match 'director'). Use spelled-out AND acronym forms. Leave blank for the built-in default (CEO, CTO, CMO, CPO, Founder/Co-Founder, Head of X, VP X, Director of X).
options.default:
CEO | CEO, Chief Executive
CTO | CTO, Chief Technology, Chief Technical
CMO | CMO, Chief Marketing
CPO | CPO, Chief Product
Founder | Founder, Co-Founder
Head | Head of
VP | VP, Vice President
Director | Director of

options.name: title_field
options.label: Item field holding the job title
options.description: Which pool-item field carries the person's title. api-fetcher maps LinkedIn `position` to `title` by default.

options.name: company_anchor
options.label: Company anchor (reject titles naming a non-target org)
options.description: When a matched title names an organisation ("Founder of SR Collection", "Head of QA at RokkerX", "VP, …, The LEGO Group") that is NOT the target company or a known alias, reject it. Aliases are derived from the roster's own company_field / company_id_field values, so "ARRISE powering Pragmatic Play" survives alongside "Pragmatic Play". Never down-weights Founder: a bare "Founder" or "Founder of <target>" always survives.

options.name: company_field
options.label: Item field holding the current company name
options.description: Used by the company anchor to derive the target-alias set. Defaults to the raw Bright Data field `current_company_name`. If the api-fetcher provider field_map renames it (e.g. to `company`), set this to match, or the anchor is inert.

options.name: company_id_field
options.label: Item field holding the current company id/slug
options.description: Second alias source for the company anchor (e.g. `current_company_company_id` = `pragmatic-play`). Defaults to the raw Bright Data field.
